svg.title: The Agent Mesh on Kubernetes: How Work Comes In and Actions Go Out
svg.desc: Read top down and left to right. Top left, outside a Kubernetes cluster, the Operator, at the command line; under the Operator, planned for v1.x, the Portal, the Operator's surface in a browser, and the Approver, another person, who uses it; both reach the Portal in a browser. The Operator calls the control API's Service, control-api, over REST, and the Portal will too; the Operator also works in Xero and in Jira, in a browser; the Portal's own Deployment, portal, is not drawn. At the top of the cluster, the Service passes the call to the control API, the Deployment control-api. The bus, the Service nats, runs from the control API down the cluster's left side. Below, two example Agents, the Book-Keeper and the Developer, each a Pod kept by its Deployment, agent-book-keeper and agent-developer, with two containers: agent-runtime, from darkwave/agent-runtime, which joins the bus and calls, over a Unix socket, its sidecar agent-mcp-gateway, from darkwave/agent-mcp-gateway, which alone holds the credentials of the install's MCP connections. Each gateway calls right, out of the cluster, over MCP and HTTPS, to its Agent's outside systems: the Book-Keeper's to Xero, accounting, Gmail, mail, and Docusign, agreements; the Developer's to GitHub, code, Slack, chat, and Jira, a tracker. Below them, a third example Agent, the Jira Watcher, an Agent with a script proposer, in a Pod of its own kept by its Deployment, agent-jira-watcher, with the same two containers; its gateway calls right, out of the cluster, over MCP and HTTPS, to Jira, to read Jira's changes, and its agent runtime publishes them on the bus as ticket.* messages. Below the Agents, planned for v1.x: the MCP server, mcp-server, which joins the bus, and the doc server, doc-server; and the webhook ingress, ingress, which joins the bus and will take Jira's webhooks. At the bottom, the config repository, a GitOps repository, is applied to the cluster on merge.
